grades.quote: If cd were run as a regular command, then the shell would fork a child process, the child process would run cd, and cd would change the _child_ ’s working directory. The parent’s (i.e., the shell’s) working directory would not change.
grades.reason: It does not directly explain why a shell does fork then exec. It does show that the shell forks a child to run a command, so changes such as the working directory affect only the child and not the shell. That gives some of the reasoning, but only through the cd example. It never mentions exec replacing the process image.

grades.quote: A process may create a new process using the fork system call. fork gives the new process an exact copy of the calling process’s memory
grades.reason: It describes fork and lists exec in the system call table, so it gives background on the primitives. It does not say why a shell forks before exec, or that exec would replace the shell itself.
